raw: {"1":"I believe economic globalization should be structured to prioritize people's wellbeing and ecological sustainability rather than corporate profit.","2":"I reject unconditional national loyalty; patriotism should be critical and tied to moral principles.","3":"I think pride in one's birthplace is understandable but should be tempered by awareness of its arbitrary origins and commitment to universal values.","4":"I strongly reject the idea that any race is superior; racial hierarchies are scientifically false and morally harmful.","5":"The saying 'the enemy of my enemy is my friend' can be tactically useful but it doesn't justify unprincipled alliances.","6":"I think military action that breaks international law is rarely justified and, if ever, must meet stringent humanitarian and legal scrutiny with full accountability.","7":"I find the fusion of information and entertainment worrying because it erodes public understanding and undermines informed civic discussion.","8":"I believe class divisions often shape people's interests more profoundly than nationality, even though both matter.","9":"I think both controlling inflation and maintaining employment are crucial, but sustained full employment should weigh heavily alongside price stability.","10":"I believe corporations need regulation to protect the environment because voluntary measures have repeatedly failed to prevent large-scale harm.","11":"I find the slogan 'from each according to his ability, to each according to his need' morally appealing as an aspiration, though practical implementation must protect liberty and incentives.","12":"I disagree that freer markets automatically mean freer people; markets require rules to prevent concentrated power and protect rights.","13":"I think it's lamentable that clean drinking water has become commodified in many places, reflecting failures in public infrastructure and governance.","14":"I don't think land should be treated purely as a commodity; stewardship, public access, and ecological limits must be considered.","15":"I regret that many fortunes are made by financial manipulation that produces little social value, and I support policies to curb rent-seeking.","16":"I accept that targeted protectionism can be necessary to nurture industries or protect security, but it should be used sparingly and transparently.","17":"I disagree that a company's only social responsibility is profit; businesses owe duties to employees, communities and the environment as well.","18":"I think whether the rich are overtaxed depends on context, but progressive taxation is justified to fund public goods and reduce extreme inequality.","19":"I believe access to high-quality medical care should be based on need rather than ability to pay, while allowing some private options under regulation.","20":"I support penalties for businesses that deliberately mislead the public because truthful information is essential for a functioning society.","21":"I agree that a genuine free market requires rules to prevent monopolies and ensure competition and fairness.","22":"I oppose making abortion always illegal when the woman's life is not threatened because reproductive autonomy and complex circumstances require nuanced law.","23":"I believe authority should always be subject to skeptical scrutiny to guard against abuse and preserve democratic accountability.","24":"I reject 'an eye for an eye' as a guiding principle because revenge perpetuates harm and undermines justice and rehabilitation.","25":"I oppose cutting all public funding for theatres and museums; cultural institutions can provide public value that justifies taxpayer support.","26":"I disagree that schools should make classroom attendance non-compulsory; compulsory education protects children's rights and equal opportunity.","27":"I reject the idea that different sorts of people should keep to their own kind; segregationist thinking damages freedom, equality and social cohesion.","28":"I don't support spanking as a routine disciplinary method because it risks physical and psychological harm and models violence rather than teaching self-control.","29":"I think it's natural and often healthy for children to keep some secrets from their parents as part of developing autonomy, within safety limits.","30":"I believe personal possession of marijuana should not be a criminal offence and should be addressed through regulation and public-health measures.","31":"I think schooling should cultivate critical thinking, civic values and diverse skills, not merely function as vocational job training.","32":"I strongly oppose denying people with inheritable disabilities the right to reproduce; reproductive freedom and human dignity must be protected against eugenics.","33":"I disagree that the most important thing for children is to accept discipline; empathy, curiosity and resilience are at least as vital.","34":"I agree that there are no 'savage' or 'civilised' peoples, only different cultures deserving respect, study and mutual understanding.","35":"I think able people should generally be expected to work, but society must provide support for those facing real barriers and hardships.","36":"I think keeping busy can help cope with trouble temporarily, but confronting and processing problems is important for long-term well-being.","37":"I disagree that first-generation immigrants can never be fully integrated; with inclusive policies and mutual adaptation many integrate successfully.","38":"I reject the notion that what's good for the biggest corporations is always good for everyone, since corporate gains often diverge from the public interest.","39":"I believe independent broadcasting can justify public funding when it serves democratic information needs, pluralism and cultural diversity.","40":"I believe many civil liberties have been unduly restricted in the name of counter-terrorism and that strong safeguards and oversight are essential.","41":"I reject the idea that a one-party state is advantageous; silencing debate undermines rights, innovation and long-term good governance.","42":"I reject the claim that only wrongdoers need to worry about surveillance; pervasive monitoring threatens everyone's privacy and freedom.","43":"I oppose the death penalty because it is irreversible, often applied unevenly, and does not provide reliable advantages over other punishments.","44":"I reject the notion that societies must always have rigid hierarchies of obedience and command; mutual respect, accountability and rights should guide social order.","45":"I think abstract art can legitimately be called art even without representation, because it can convey ideas, emotions and formal insight.","46":"I disagree that punishment should trump rehabilitation in criminal justice; reducing reoffending and restoring victims requires focus on rehabilitation alongside proportionate sanctions.","47":"I acknowledge some offenders are hard to rehabilitate, but I don't think trying to rehabilitate is a waste of time because it reduces harm and long-term costs.","48":"I don't accept that businesspeople are more important than writers and artists; a healthy society needs both economic activity and cultural creativity.","49":"I reject the claim that mothers' first duty is homemaking; parents should be free to choose roles with societal support for caregiving and work.","50":"I think climate science rightly warns that limitless material growth is incompatible with stabilising the climate, so we must pursue sustainable, equitable economic models.","51":"I think maturity doesn't require making peace with the establishment if doing so abandons core principles; maturity can mean principled engagement and compromise when warranted.","52":"I don't believe astrology explains many things reliably; it lacks evidence and shouldn't guide important personal or public decisions.","53":"I disagree that you cannot be moral without being religious; secular ethical systems can support deep moral commitments and civic responsibility.","54":"I believe social security provides a more reliable and equitable foundation for supporting the disadvantaged than relying primarily on charity.","55":"I accept that luck affects people's outcomes, so policy should address bad luck with safety nets rather than moralizing individuals.","56":"I think it's appropriate for schools to respect families' religious values while ensuring public education remains inclusive, secular and rights
